content.thinking:
I'm planning the qilin's proportions and design carefully to avoid runtime errors, aiming for a horse-sized quadruped with jade-teal scales, gold accents, cream tones, and a flowing cloud-like mane.

Building the skeleton chain...

I'll use a decal approach for the eyes, placing them on the skull sphere via spherical coordinates with azimuth controlling left/right mirroring. For antlers, I'm planning branching sweeps per side with a main beam curving back and up from the skull top, plus smaller tines.

For positioning, I need to settle the left/right convention—model left corresponds to +X—then decide to just define absolute head coordinates as constants rather than relying on relative local offsets, to keep things simpler.

I'm working through the creature's absolute anatomy: skull around [0,1.88,1.2], snout tapering to a nose tip near z=1.62, antlers rising toward 2.35 for a horse-sized frame. Then I reconsider scale and lower the whole thing—hips at y=1.0, shoulders at 1.1, neck end and head center around 1.62, antlers topping out near 2.05—to get proportions that feel right.

Now I'm mapping the body out as a spine path through catmull points, planning to build separate swept tubes for body, neck, and tail rather than one continuous mesh, with varying radii for chest, waist, and hips, and overlapping caps to hide the seams at the neck base. I'm setting up the spine joint chain parented to the hips to drive this structure.

Then I'm defining the body sweep radius function along the spine and layering the scale paint with a cream countershade for the belly, wrapped in cel shading for a toon look.

I'm deciding to keep the body as one smooth sweep with rounded caps rather than adding extra hip or rump spheres, just a chest sphere for shape. Now I'm setting up the front legs using inverse kinematics, placing the shoulder joint and foot target positions.

For the leg segments, I'm working out lengths for a three-segment limb (shoulder-elbow, forearm, cannon) that reaches from hip height to the ground, and figuring out which direction each joint should bend—elbow pointing backward, wrist pointing forward—to match natural horse-like leg posture.

Adjusting leg segment lengths to 1.08 total with forward knee bend and backward hock bend, naming the four-point chain hip-knee-hock-hoof. Sweeping tubes along each leg with tapering radii, bulkier at the thigh, and capping the hoof with a small cone shape at the tip joint.

I'm skipping fetlock sprite hair for now and planning to add flame-tuft card textures on the legs and cloud-textured mane later. For the tail, I'm sketching a curved catmull-rom chain of points drooping down and back from the rump, aiming for that stylized qilin tail shape.

Now I'm thinking about the cloud mane along the neck, using overlapping circle puffs with spiral wisps in white/teal/gold, placed as cards that follow the neck's curve and leaning back at an angle, spread across three angles for fuller volume.

I'm extending that coverage to cheeks, chest ruff, spine, and leg joints, plus adding a few spiral cloud-scroll shapes at the shoulders and hips with gold edges for extra flair. Writing SVG gradient code...

I'm planning texture variants (teal-white, pink-lavender, gold wisps) for variety across cards, then sketching head anatomy: a jade skull sphere, gold brow spikes, snout with nostrils and a cream lip, lower jaw with a goatee tuft, fang spikes, and ear shapes.

Still designing ear geometry...

Now I'm working out antler colors—gold-cream for the beams with glowing cyan tips—and plotting the antler beam path curving upward and outward from the skull base.

Adding tip spheres with a glow effect for the antler ends, setting flat-to-point caps on the sweep with rigid bone binding to the head joint. I'm sketching whiskers too, sweeping a thin catmull curve from the snout sides outward with golden color and pointed caps.

Now I'm working on eye placement, sizing the decals relative to the skull's width and figuring out the correct azimuth and elevation angles so they land on the forward-facing side of the skull, using the hit normal for orientation.

For the chimera build, I'm adding hooves, fetlock tufts, lion tail, deer body, ox hooves, dragon head, and scaled texturing, then trying to wrap a golden collar ring around the neck base by finding the right joint point and loop direction so it doesn't accidentally snap to the chest geometry instead.

Now thinking about adding gold dorsal ridge spikes along the body sweep for texture, plus considering scale patches, belly markings, and flank decal swirls to give the body more surface detail.

No mirror needed. Drafting the spiral path for the swirl decal with gold stroke curves plus cloud lobe circles around it, then moving on to add gold wrist bands on the legs.

For the leg anklet, I'm positioning the loop cut at the wrist joint, orienting it perpendicular to the bone axis so the gold band wraps cleanly around the leg surface.

For glowing elements, I'm only applying glow to the antler tips and gems, not the eyes. I'm also double-checking my imports to make sure I only bring in modules actually used, avoiding unused imports like offset that would trigger a typecheck error.

Now I'm defining the color palette: jade greens for the main body with lighter and darker edge tones, cream and gold accents, antler and tip colors, plus cloud white, pink, lavender, and hoof tones.

Working out the coat and belly textures, I'm using scaled gradients for the main scales versus a creamier gradient for the belly sectors, and considering how to handle leg coloring with a transition toward cream at the lower legs.

Still writing paint and shape definitions...

Still positioning head geometry...

Adding goatee wisp cards hanging down from the jaw frame, then setting up a cheek ruff using scattered points off the skull surface, filtering for side-facing normals and tying each wisp card to the jaw bone with a backward lean.

For the neck mane I'm placing cards along the neck tube at multiple clock angles around the dorsal axis for volume, since the neck tilts roughly 45 degrees forward. Then I'm extending a thinner line of mane cards along the back down toward the tail, tapering their size as they go.

For the tail, I'm building a tuft near the tip using cards following the tail's tangent frames for a swept look, then adding a ring of outward-facing cards partway along the tail to fan out like a flame, varying size and lean to give it a wispy, cloud-like end.

Now I'm thinking through fetlock tufts using a ring around the leg at a point near the hoof, with cards leaning down and flattened flow so they lie along the surface, keeping sizes small. I'm noting that `b.ring()` returns items I need to access via `.items`, and considering skipping hair behind the knee while weighing whether to add floating cloud swirls at the hooves.

Skipping cloud puffs under the hooves since they'd need to float above floor level, and skipping a gold chest plate too, keeping just a collar and gem. Now I'm designing a leaf-shaped fin at the elbow pointing backward, working out an outline of points that avoids self-intersection.

Now I'm working through the leg joint bone extrusion with gold coloring, then moving to eye sockets using the skull surface, and sketching the brow sweep curves above the eye.

Checking the brow points stay roughly within the skull surface, then placing eyes, ears, and antler bases relative to the skull geometry, working out the beam path coordinates for the antlers.

Defining branch points for the tines along the antler beam, each specifying where along the beam they sprout, their direction vector, and length, ready to feed into a recursive branching function.

Adding more geometry details...

Defining body barrel radii...

Now I'm placing shoulder and hip joints for front and hind legs, computing limb targets, and checking that leg segment lengths are sufficient to reach the ground given the distances involved.

Checking that the leg structure uses a points array passed directly to the chain builder, then sweeping a tube along it with a tapering radius array for visual thickness toward the paw. Now I'm figuring out where to place the elbow joint.

Now I'm working out the chimera's flame-like shoulder and hip wisps, placing swirl cards at symmetric angles along the body tube with varying sizes and lean, reasoning through clockwise orientation as seen looking toward +Z to get left/right placement correct.

I'm also sketching the limb coloring pass, deciding to skip a cheek decal, and applying the cel-shaded scale coloring with a base/edge color array. For the jaw joint, I'm anchoring it relative to the neck's endpoint and aim direction so it connects naturally to the head.

Adding the skull bone part with a small sphere, then setting up scattered cheek details filtered by position and normal direction, with sizing, lean, flow, and tint parameters.

Writing a helper that generates wispy flame-like SVG shapes...

Finishing the swirl decal paths and adding small gold circle accents, then I'm calculating the exact surface position for placing the decal based on the body's radius at that point along the curve.

I'm defining the leg cuffs as swept loop paths around the tube's surface, placing small nostril and nose-bulb spheres near the muzzle, and confirming the part count stays well under budget.

Now I'm working on whiskers as paired sweeps per side, setting up a lambda for mane card distribution, and defining goatee frames anchored near the jaw with explicit bone binding for the card placement calls.

I'm also building out tube sweeps for the neck and tail, drawing frames from each tube's parametric points, pulling in a glow effect import, and sketching the color palette along with the final metadata block for the piece.

Checking the tuft cards angle outward from the tail axis with tilt toward the tail direction to create a flared brush look, then confirming vertical extents—antlers topping around 2.35, hooves sitting at floor level. I'm also placing a golden forehead gem near the skull's front top area.

Now I'm computing precise gem placement using the skull's ellipsoid surface equation to ensure it sits just outside the surface, settling on coordinates near [0, 1.745, 1.365] with a small cyan glow radius. Then I'm writing out the part definitions, using a side array for left/right symmetry and naming conventions, and preparing to assemble the full file.
